title: Fair Share: Fractions and Equal Sharing

standard_text: Fractions: sharing equally, half, one-third, one-fourth of shapes and collections, and comparing simple fractions (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 Fair Share worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 8): equal shares, halves, thirds and quarters, fractions of a group, comparing. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A fraction names equal parts of a whole: 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts.
  • 1/4 of 12 rotis: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
  • More equal parts make each part smaller: 1/4 < 1/2.

Examples

Example

What is 1/3 of 15?

15 ÷ 3

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling unequal parts halvesHalves must be the same size.
Thinking 1/4 is bigger than 1/34 parts are smaller than 3 parts.

faq.a: Sharing so everyone gets exactly the same amount.

items.q: 12 muffins are shared equally by 4 friends. How many muffins does each friend get?
items.e: Share 12 muffins into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Each person gets 3 muffins.

items.q: 15 oranges are shared equally by 5 friends. How many oranges does each friend get?
items.e: Share 15 oranges into 5 equal groups: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Each person gets 3 oranges.

items.q: 16 granola bars are shared equally by 8 friends. How many granola bars does each friend get?
items.e: Share 16 granola bars into 8 equal groups: 16 ÷ 8 = 2. Each person gets 2 granola bars.

items.q: 18 brownies are shared equally by 6 friends. How many brownies does each friend get?
items.e: Share 18 brownies into 6 equal groups: 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Each person gets 3 brownies.

items.q: 1 pizza is shared equally by 6 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut the pizza into 6 equal pieces (sixths). Each person gets 1 piece: 16 of a pizza.

items.q: 2 sandwiches are shared equally by 3 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much of a sandwich does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each sandwich into 3 equal pieces (thirds). Each person gets 1 piece from each sandwich. There are 2 sandwiches, so each person gets 23 of a sandwich.

items.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each pizza into 4 equal pieces (fourths). Each person gets 1 piece from each pizza. There are 3 pizzas, so each person gets 34 of a pizza.

items.q: 2 granola bars are shared equally by 5 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much of a granola bar does each friend get?

items.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally by 6 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each pizza into 6 equal pieces (sixths). Each person gets 1 piece from each pizza. There are 5 pizzas, so each person gets 56 of a pizza.

items.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 8 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each pizza into 8 equal pieces (eighths). Each person gets 1 piece from each pizza. There are 3 pizzas, so each person gets 38 of a pizza.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 14 = 13
14 > 13
14 < 13
items.e: Both fractions have 1 on top. A whole cut into 3 parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 4 parts. So 14 < 13.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the largest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The smallest bottom number means the biggest parts. 12 is the largest.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the smallest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The biggest bottom number means the smallest parts. 18 is the smallest.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Harsh eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza does he eat?
items.e: The pizza has 8 equal slices, so the denominator is 8. Harsh eats 3, so the answer is 38.

items.q: A bar of chocolate has 5 equal pieces. Rohan eats 2 pieces. What fraction of the bar is left?
items.e: 5 − 2 = 3 pieces are left out of 5 equal pieces. The answer is 35.

items.q: There are 30 children in a Class 3. 13 of them have school dinners. How many children have school dinners?
items.e: Share 30 into 3 equal groups: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 children. One group is 13.

items.q: Manav has 20 sweets. 34 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: First find 14: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. You need 3 groups, not 1: 5 × 3 = 15 sweets.

items.q: There are 24 students in a class. 38 of them go to football club. How many students go to football club?
items.e: First find 18: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. You need 3 groups, not 1: 3 × 3 = 9 students.

items.q: Aditya and 3 friends share 3 pizzas equally at a birthday party. How much pizza does each person get?
items.e: Aditya and 3 friends are 4 people. Cut each pizza into fourths. Each person gets 1 piece from each of the 3 pizzas: 34 of a pizza.

items.q: Anika and Nikhil share 5 pancakes equally at breakfast. How many pancakes does each child get?
items.e: 5 ÷ 2 = 2 each, with 1 pancake left. Cut it into halves. Each child gets 2 12 pancakes.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 3 friends share 2 granola bars equally. How much of a granola bar does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each granola bar into thirds. Each friend gets 1 third from each bar: 13 + 13 = 23.

items.q: Siddharth and 3 friends share 20 hockey cards equally. How many cards does each person get?
items.e: Siddharth and 3 friends are 4 people. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cards each.

items.q: At hockey practice, 8 players share 5 oranges equally. How much orange does each player get?
items.e: Cut each orange into eighths. Each player gets 1 piece from each of the 5 oranges: 58 of an orange.

items.q: On a field trip, 4 students share 7 sandwiches equally. How many sandwiches does each student get?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 each, with 3 sandwiches left. Cut each one into fourths. Each student gets 3 more fourths: 1 34 sandwiches.

items.q: After football, 4 players share 9 muffins equally. How many muffins does each player get?
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 each, with 1 muffin left. Cut it into fourths. Each player gets 2 14 muffins.

items.q: Arjun shares 3 subs equally with 4 friends. How much of a sub does each person get?
items.e: Arjun and 4 friends are 5 people. Cut each sub into fifths. Each person gets 1 piece from each sub: 35 of a sub.

items.q: 10 friends share 3 pizzas equally. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each pizza into tenths. Each friend gets 1 piece from each of the 3 pizzas: 310 of a pizza.

items.q: At a class party, 10 students share 12 pizzas equally. Does each student get more or less than 1 pizza?
items.e: There are more pizzas than students. Each student gets 1 pizza. The 2 pizzas left are cut into tenths, so each student gets 1 210 pizzas.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Zoya eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal slices, so the denominator is 4. Zoya eats 1, so the answer is 14.

items.q: A family pizza is cut into 10 equal slices. The family eats 7 slices. What fraction of the pizza is left?

items.q: A block of chocolate has 20 equal squares. Vivaan eats 15 of the block. How many squares does he eat?

items.q: There are 30 students in a Class 3. 110 of them walk to school. How many students walk to school?

items.q: There are 30 students in a class. 13 of them ride a bike to school. How many students ride a bike?

items.q: The school sausage sizzle has 40 sausages. 110 of them are vegetarian. How many vegetarian sausages are there?

items.q: Lakshmi has 12 strawberries for recess. She gives 13 of them to a friend. How many does she give away?
items.e: Share 12 into 3 equal groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 strawberries. One group is 13.

items.q: Ayaan eats 25 of a cake. Isha eats the rest. What fraction of the cake does Isha eat?
items.e: The whole cake is 55. 55 − 25 = 35, because 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: A watermelon is cut into 4 equal pieces. Pooja and Siddharth each eat 1 piece. What fraction of the watermelon is left?
items.e: They eat 2 pieces, 14 + 14 = 24. 4 − 2 = 2 pieces are left, so 24 is left.

items.q: On a school excursion, the class walks 1 km to the park. They have walked 610 of the way. What fraction of the way is left?
items.e: The whole walk is 1010. 10 − 6 = 4, so 410 of the way is left.
